# Occasion and audience

## What this deck is made for

- Occasion: handing a mapped control over to engineering, before the
  implementation
- Audience: `engineering`
- Length: 30 minutes, on a number that is currently due
- What the audience already knows: their own systems; no prior knowledge of the
  management system needed

::: {.notes}
This slide is not presented. There is a second deck for this topic, for the
practitioners. This one is not its short version: it starts at a single number
and does not go through the procedure.
:::

# What it is about

## The subject in one sentence

Behind every number of the annex stands an intention, and ISO/IEC 27002 says
what matters when it is put in place.

## Why it concerns engineering

- What gets implemented arrives as a number, and a number alone does not say
  when it is met
- Without the intention behind it an implementation arises that fits formally
  and lowers no risk
- The question how it is recognised that it works comes later anyway, and then
  without preparation

# A number arrives

## What has to arrive with it

- The number itself, say 5.18 or 8.16
- The risk row it comes from, in one sentence
- Who answers for the consequences

## What to do before building

- Read up on what matters for this number, in a licensed copy
- Check whether the intention matches the purpose or only its name
- Ask back where the intention settles more than the number does, or less

# How it is recognised that it works

## The evidence is planned with it

- Every implementation comes with an observation showing that it runs
- It arises while building and not in the audit
- ISO/IEC 27001:2022, 9.1, asks for the evaluation; the figure for it has to
  arise somewhere

## Two forms that are enough

- A record that arises without anyone thinking about it
- A look back at a fixed interval whose result is written down
- Both with a date, otherwise it is a memory and not evidence

# What engineering does not decide

## Three boundaries

- Whether a control is applied: the risk treatment decides that
- Whether a number is dropped: the reason for that is the risk situation and
  stands in the statement of applicability
- What stands in the standard: the wording is looked up in a licensed copy and
  not passed on second hand

## The list is not the starting point

- The annex does not get worked through from top to bottom
- A number with no risk row behind it is effort without a reason
- Anyone receiving such a number asks for the row

# What to do or decide afterwards

## The next steps

- Fetch the risk row for the number that is due, where it is missing
- Describe the implementation and beside it the observation that evidences it
- Name the point at which the implementation settles more than the number, and
  report it back
- Who, by when: belongs in the discussion and not on this slide

# References

## Standard, clause and edition

- ISO/IEC 27002:2022, as a whole standard
- ISO/IEC 27001:2022, 6.1.3
- ISO/IEC 27001:2022, 8.1
- ISO/IEC 27001:2022, 9.1
- ISO/IEC 27004:2016, as a whole standard

No standard wording, no control title and no enumeration of the annex numbers
stands on these slides. The two numbers named stand as an example of the form
and without the title that stands behind them in the standard.
